companyDescription: Psychedelic psychiatry · COMP360 psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression — two positive Phase 3s (COMP005, COMP006), NDA COMPLETED Nov 9, 2026 with a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (1–2 month review target) · potential first FDA-approved psilocybin therapy, launch targeted H1 2027 pending DEA rescheduling
priceNote: Live $8.08 (+1.25%) on Nov 18, 2026 (live-prices cache) — -13% since the Nov 11 report ($9.25) with the small-cap tape. The final COMP360 NDA was completed on Nov 9 (the Nov 11 report's ~Nov 17 catalyst is resolved), and the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher targets a 1–2 month review.
summary: Refresh — the Nov 11 report's catalyst resolved on schedule: Compass completed its COMP360 NDA for treatment-resistant depression on Nov 9, backed by two positive Phase 3s (COMP005, COMP006) plus a Phase 2b in >1,000 participants. Its Commissioner's National Priority Voucher targets a 1–2 month review, so an FDA decision could land ~Jan 2027 — inside the turbo window. The stock still fell 13% to $8.08 with the tape. The scheduling hurdle remains: DEA and states must reschedule psilocybin before launch (targeted H1 2027). Targets are unchanged (HCW $65 down to Wells Fargo $10). The turbo at-catalyst median is -6.6% (n=76), so Entry 2 is preferred. แนะนำ 2–3% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้าได้ CRL ลงได้ 40–50%.

catalysts.name: FDA decision on COMP360 (priority voucher review)
catalysts.description: The NDA was completed on Nov 9, 2026. Compass holds a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher; its CCO said a potential benefit is a review of one to two months after final submission. No action date has been published, so the window is ~Dec 2026–Jan 2027.

catalysts.name: DEA rescheduling + U.S. launch
catalysts.description: COMP360 contains a Schedule I substance, so DEA and individual states must reschedule it before commercialization. The company targets a potential U.S. launch in H1 2027, contingent on approval.

risks: FDA could refuse to file or later issue a CRL. Functional unblinding, durability and REMS/monitoring design are known psychedelic review issues (Lykos MDMA CRL, 2024).
The effect size has disappointed before: CMPS fell ~36% on COMP005 in Jun 2025 despite hitting the primary endpoint.
Commercial model risk: in-clinic dosing with monitoring needs certified sites and a reimbursement path, so the launch ramp may be slow.
Warrant overhang and the likelihood of a raise around approval.
Timing: the 1–2 month priority-voucher review is a target, not a statutory date — it could slip, and DEA rescheduling still gates any launch.

estimateDates.note: Priority-voucher review, 1–2 months after the Nov 9 submission

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds 3.75–4.00% after the Sep 16 hike. CME FedWatch prices a +25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC at ~95% (Nov 17–18), with the remainder on 50bp. Waller has floated 50bp; Williams pushed back.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Oct CPI ran hot (core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2%). Sep core PCE 3.1% y/y. Oct PCE (Nov 25) and Nov CPI (Dec 10) are next.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Pre-commercial CNS biotech moving toward launch. Funded (~$444M), so rates matter through biotech multiples rather than financing needs.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — macro is WAIT (30/100): the S&P closed Nov 17 on its 200-day at a 5-month low with VIX ~23–26. The outcome here is idiosyncratic, but small-cap biotech sells first on a hot PCE, so use the dip entry.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE · Moonshot 2.5% max — the NDA is in with a priority voucher, so the binary FDA decision has moved up to ~Jan 2027. The measured turbo at-catalyst median is -6.6% (n=76), so Entry 2 ($7.40–7.90) is preferred and Entry 1 is a starter only.

catalystSpot.preRunup: CMPS is already moving: +7.7% on Nov 11 with HCW reiterating $65. Filing news is largely expected, and the bigger re-rating historically comes at acceptance and approval.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: Into the filing PR (~Nov 17) and the 60-day acceptance

postWin.note: AXSM rose ~40% on the Auvelity (depression) approval after a long review (Aug 2022). SRPT closed +74% on the eteplirsen accelerated approval (Sep 2016). Novel-mechanism CNS approvals re-rate sharply when the market had priced in doubt.

postLose.note: CMPS itself fell ~36% on underwhelming COMP005 effect size (Jun 2025). A CRL or refuse-to-file would plausibly be -40–50% for a pre-commercial single-asset company.

spotSizing.reason: 2.5%. regulatory_approval is at +5.8pp medianExcess vs +7.7pp overall (n=23), not a laggard. Lane-wide prior (hitRate 6.5%, softHitRate 27.1%, beatBench 71%, n=107) and a WAIT macro tape (30/100) keep turbo sizing at the low end of 2–5%.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the turbo medianMAE (-20%). A break below ~$6.05 before the event means the market is pricing a bad outcome.

stopPostCatalyst.note: Refuse-to-file or a CRL means exit immediately. Do not average down into a resubmission cycle.

comparableCases.event: FDA approves Auvelity for MDD after an extended review
comparableCases.note: Depression approval after the market had priced in rejection risk. This is the template for a COMP360 approval re-rating.
Controversial first-in-class approval. The stock had priced in doubt and closed +74%, the upper bound for a contested regulatory win.
